texts.title: Out of the Line
texts.body: Your fleet has won the day, and the dispatches all say the same thing: {officer.name} did not wait for the signal. They took their ships out of the line, round the enemy's flank, and the enemy broke. It won the battle. It was also against orders, and the whole fleet saw it. What you write now is what the Reach will read.

choices.take_the_credit: Let the dispatch say it was your plan.

texts.title: The Officer Who Ran
texts.body: The battle is lost, and the reports agree on one thing. Before the line broke, {officer.name} pulled their ships out of it and made for home. The line broke after. Whether it would have held if they had stayed, nobody can say; the crews are already saying it would.

choices.cover_for_them: Write the report so the line broke somewhere else.

texts.title: A Laurel at the Peace
texts.body: The war is over, and the Senate is drawing up its list of those who served. Each house puts its own names forward. {officer.name} is owed something for the war, and everyone in the house knows it, {officer.name} most of all.

choices.name_them_to_the_senate: Put {officer.name}'s name to the Senate (1 influence).
choices.a_purse: Give them a purse from the house (300 credits).

texts.title: The Other Dispatch
texts.body: The war is over, and {officer.name} has written their own account of the battle. It does not say what yours said. Whatever has passed between you since, they have not forgotten what was said of them then. It is being copied and read in the city, in the wardrooms and in the Senate's corridors, and people are asking you which one is true.

choices.answer_it: Answer it in the Senate (1 influence).

texts.title: A Place in the Fleet
texts.body: {kin.name} is young, and the war is all anyone in the house talks about. They have come to ask you for a place aboard the house's fleet. They have it all worked out: what they will do, who they will serve under. They have not worked out what you will feel when the reports come in.

choices.send_them: Send {kin.name} aboard the house's fleet. A battle lost may cost them.
choices.take_them_on_your_staff: Take {kin.name} onto your own staff. A battle lost may cost them.
choices.a_safe_post: Find them a post at the yards (1 influence).

texts.title: Blooded in Battle
texts.body: The house's fleet has been in action, and {kin.name} was in it. They came through. What they say of it is short, and they do not say it the way they did when they went.

choices.a_step_up: Ask the Admiralty to give {kin.name} a step. They stay with the fleet.
choices.bring_them_home: Bring {kin.name} home now they have seen it.
choices.leave_them_with_the_fleet: Leave them with the fleet. A battle lost may still cost them.

texts.title: Wounded Aboard the Fleet
texts.body: The house's fleet has lost a battle, and {kin.name}, whom you sent to the front, is among the wounded. The dispatch is short. It says they are asking to stay at their post, and that the fleet's surgeons have more wounded than they can see to.

choices.bring_them_home_to_mend: Bring {kin.name} home to mend. They will not thank you for it.
choices.send_the_house_physician: Send the house's own physician out to them (300 credits). They stay with the fleet.
choices.leave_them_to_the_surgeons: Leave them to the fleet's surgeons, like everyone else's. A battle lost may cost them again.

texts.title: Home From the War
texts.body: The war is over, and {kin.name} is home. They went out young and eager, and they have come back thinner and quieter, with the habits of the fleet and nothing yet to put them to. The house is glad to have them. What {kin.name} wants from you now, they have not said.

choices.a_feast_for_them: Give a feast for their homecoming (400 credits).
choices.a_place_in_the_service: Ask the Admiralty to give them a step (1 influence).
choices.let_them_be: Let them be, and ask nothing.
choices.ask_what_they_saw: Ask them what they saw, all of it. It will not be easy for them.

texts.title: Taken in Battle
texts.body: Among those pulled from the wrecks of {prisoner.house}'s line is {prisoner.name}, {prisoner.rankName}, who commanded one of their ships. They are held under guard aboard the house's flagship. {prisoner.house} will want them back, and will remember how they came home.

choices.exchange_them: Exchange them for your own crews they hold.
choices.parole_them: Let them go on their word not to fight you again in this war.

texts.title: The Parole Broken in the Line
texts.body: {parolee.name} gave you their word not to fight you again in this war, and you let them go on it. {parolee.house} has given them a fleet, and it is in the line against yours.

choices.send_a_herald: Send a herald to say it to their face.
choices.let_it_go: Let it go: it is a war.

texts.title: Deserters From the Fleet
texts.body: Crews have left one of the house's fleets this year: a hull's worth of them, gone over the side at a port of call with whatever they could carry. A good many have been taken since, at ports of your own, and they are in the cells waiting to hear what the house will do with them. The crews still aboard are waiting to hear it too.

choices.hang_them: Hang them where they were taken. The officers will approve; the commons will not.
choices.take_them_back: Take them back into the fleet, flogged and unpaid. The officers will think it soft.
choices.pay_what_they_were_owed: Pay them what they were owed and let them go (300 credits). The commons will think the better of the house for it.
choices.send_them_to_the_yards: Send them to work in the house's yards under guard. The towns will grumble.

texts.title: A Parley Before the Fleets Meet
texts.body: {foe.name} of {foe.house} has a fleet a year out from yours, under way and coming. Their herald is aboard the house's flagship with a request: before the guns, will you meet them? Commanders have talked before battles for as long as there have been battles. Sometimes there is no battle afterwards.

choices.offer_a_white_peace: Offer a white peace: nothing changes hands.
choices.meet_under_a_truce: Meet under a flag of truce, and fight when they come. The wardroom will not like it.
choices.count_their_ships: Use the parley to count their ships. Their fleet will fight the worse for it.
choices.send_the_herald_back: Send the herald back unheard. The wardroom will cheer it.

texts.title: Plunder on the Exchange
texts.body: {sacker.house}'s fleet is home from beyond the rim. It sacked a world out there and came back with its holds full, and {sacker.name} is selling what it carried: metals, stores, worked things from a world that is not theirs. Plunder sells fast and cheap. {sacker.name} has sent word that {sacker.house} will sail again, and has room for a partner.

choices.buy_from_the_plunder: Buy from the plunder (500 credits): two lots of metals and a crate of exotics, at half what the Exchange asks.
choices.put_money_into_the_next_raid: Put money into their next raid (300 credits).
choices.call_for_a_tax_on_plunder: Ask the Senate for a tax on plunder (1 influence).
choices.have_nothing_to_do_with_it: Have nothing to do with it.

texts.title: A Scandal in the Accounts
texts.body: The war beyond the rim is over, and the money you put into {partner.house}'s raids has come back, with a good deal more. So have the Senate's auditors, who are going through the plunder of the war, house by house. Your name is in {partner.name}'s books.

choices.keep_it: Keep the 800 credits, and say nothing.
choices.give_it_to_the_crews: Give it to the families of the crews.
choices.share_it_with_the_auditor: Share it with the auditor, and keep 500 credits. An auditor of the Senate will know what the house is.

texts.title: The Crews Want Paying
texts.body: The war is over and the crews are coming home: men and women who have done nothing for years but fight, more of them than the peace has work for. The quays are full of them. They are owed their pay, and someone has to find it: the house's treasury, the people of its worlds, or nobody.

choices.pay_them_off: Pay them off in full from the treasury (600 credits). The officers will drink to it.
choices.settle_them: Settle them on the house's worlds (200 credits). The commons will be glad of them.
choices.a_war_tax: Lay a war tax on the people of your worlds to pay them. The crews are paid; the commons will hate it.
choices.turn_them_loose: Turn them loose unpaid. Neither the officers nor the towns will forgive it.
